About Renalytix

Renalytix (LSE: RENX) (OTCQB: RNLXY) is an artificial intelligence-enabled
in vitro
diagnostics company, focused on optimizing clinical management of kidney disease to drive improved patient outcomes. Renalytix has received FDA approval and Medicare reimbursement for
kidneyintelX.dkd
which is now offered commercially in the United States.
Unrecognized and uncontrolled diabetic kidney disease remains one of the largest barriers to controlling cost and suffering in the United States and the United Kingdom’s medical system, affecting approximately 15 million and 8 million people, respectively. After five years of development and clinical validation,
kidneyintelX.dkd
is the only FDA-approved and Medicare-reimbursed prognostic tool capable of understanding a patient’s risk with diabetic kidney disease early where treatment has maximal effect.
kidneyintelX.dkd
is now being deployed across large physician group practices and health systems in select regions of the United States.
The over 15,000 patients that have been tested by
kidneyintelX.dkd
have produced a substantial body of real-world performance data. In patient populations where
kidneyintelX.dkd
has been deployed, a demonstrated and significant increase in diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment rates have been recorded.
kidneyintelX.dkd
now has full reimbursement established by Medicare, the largest insurance payer in the United States, at $950 per reportable result.
kidneyintelX.dkd
is also recommended for use in the international chronic kidney disease clinical guidelines (KDIGO).
KidneyIntelX
is based on technology developed by Mount Sinai faculty and licensed to Renalytix AI, Inc. Mount Sinai faculty members are co-founders and equity owners in the Company. In addition, the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai has equity ownership in Renalytix. For information about the kidneyintelX,dkd test, visit
kidneyintelx.com
.

Change of Accounting Reference Date
Renalytix plc (LSE: RENX) (OTCQB: RNLXY), a precision medicine diagnostics company focussed on kidney disease,
announces that it has resolved to change the Company's accounting reference date.
The Company's financial year
‑
end will change from 30 June to 31 December.
Accordingly:

Following the Company's audited results for the year ended 30 June 2025, the current accounting period has been extended and will now end on 31 December 2026, resulting in an 18
‑
month accounting period.

The Company published interim results for the six
‑
month period ended 31 December 2025 in March 2026.

The Company will publish unaudited interim results for the 12
‑
month period ending 30 June 2026 in late October 2026.

The Company will publish audited accounts for the 18
‑
month period ending 31 December 2026 no later than 30 June 2027, in accordance with AIM Rule 19.

Thereafter, the Company will report on a 12
‑
month financial year ending 31 December, with interim results covering the six months to 30 June each year.
The Board believes that the change in accounting reference date will better align the Company's financial reporting with its operational and strategic planning cycle. Following the recently announced multi-year partnership with Quest Diagnostics (“Quest”),
kidneyintelX.dkd
is expected to be available for physician ordering through Quest's system in the first quarter of 2027. As a result, the Company is increasingly using the calendar year as the basis for forecasting, budgeting, and evaluating commercial performance.
The change to a 31 December year-end will therefore better align the Company's external financial reporting with its internal budgeting and forecasting processes and the expected timing of the next phase of its commercial growth.

company_30s.what_they_do: Renalytix plc develops precision‑medicine diagnostic tests that detect kidney disease early and help doctors tailor treatment. Their main product line includes a panel of biomarkers that can be run on a standard blood sample.
company_30s.why_they_matter: Kidney disease is a growing global health problem, and early detection can reduce costs and improve outcomes. Renalytix has a partnership with Quest Diagnostics that gives it access to a vast laboratory network, positioning it to scale its tests and capture a share of the expanding diagnostics market.
company_30s.current_state: The company is still building its revenue base and is actively raising capital. It has a very small market cap and trades at a penny‑level price, indicating it is still in a high‑cash‑burn phase but with a clear growth narrative.

rns_narrative: The firm is in the midst of a fundraising push, with multiple notices of capital‑access windows, a wrap retail offer, and a proposed fundraise all announced in September. This shows it is actively seeking liquidity to fund R&D and commercialisation.
A strategic partnership with Quest Diagnostics was announced in early September, signalling a path to scale the test kit into a large laboratory network.
Corporate governance updates, such as the AGM notice and the new accounting reference date, suggest the board is preparing for increased scrutiny and a potential market‑listing event.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet optimism – the chatter is low but the buzz is around funding and a big partnership.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bulls point to the Quest deal and the CEO’s share purchase as evidence that insiders believe the business is on a path to growth.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears worry that the capital‑raise will dilute existing shareholders, that the company still has no clear path to profitability, and that the WRAP retail offer may dilute further.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The tone has shifted from cautious to mildly hopeful after the partnership news, but overall engagement remains low.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends is flat, meaning the market has not yet noticed the story – a perfect set‑up for surprise.

near_term_catalysts: If the Quest Diagnostics integration becomes operational, volume could jump as the test is rolled out across labs.
The completion of the September capital‑raise will extend the cash runway and signal investor confidence.
A regulatory approval or a positive real‑world evidence study release will validate the test’s clinical utility and open new sales channels.
The WRAP retail offer finalisation could bring in a wave of new retail investors, pushing the price higher.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a volume spike of >10,000 shares and a break of the 2‑p support level. A clear announcement of the partnership’s launch or a funding close will confirm the thesis. A sudden drop in volume or a negative regulatory comment would be a red flag.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock sits in the early recovery phase of a deep crash. The APEX score (high) suggests a tight compression, so a breakout above the key support is the trigger to consider entering.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The company is a classic deep‑crash play – it’s fallen far below its intrinsic value. A bounce to the midpoint of its all‑time high would deliver a 4‑to‑5× return, while the downside is limited to the current price. The partnership with Quest and the ongoing capital raise provide tangible catalysts for a mean‑reversion move.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: If the fundraising fails or the partnership stalls, the company could remain stuck in a cash‑burn cycle. Dilution from the WRAP retail offer could further erode shareholder value, and a lack of profitability could keep the price languishing near the floor.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Risk is capped at the current price level; upside could be 4‑5×. The asymmetry is clear: a small loss if the price stays flat, a large gain if the partnership and funding materialise.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter when the price clears the 2‑p support with volume above 10,000 shares. Allocate 10 % of capital to the position, place a stop just below 1 p, and trail the stop upward as the price climbs.
playbook.if_watching: Hold cash until you see a clear partnership launch or a funding close. Trigger an entry if the price moves above 3 p on a volume spike of >20,000 shares.
playbook.if_passing: None – there are no imminent delisting or bankruptcy risks identified.

ai_insights.bottom_line: The stock sits at a deep trough; a partnership launch or funding close could spark a mean‑reversion rally with 4‑5× upside and limited downside – a textbook contrarian bullish setup.
